name: Pet Emergency Kit Checklist
description: A checklist to help pet owners stock a complete first aid kit and a disaster go-bag so they are ready for any emergency.

items.text: Gauze pads and rolls for wounds
Non-stick bandages and adhesive tape
Blunt-tipped scissors and tweezers
Digital thermometer and disposable gloves
Saline solution and a pet-safe wound cleaner
items.note: Ask your vet what to add for your pet's needs

items.text: A few days of any prescription medicines
Flea, tick, and parasite prevention on hand
Written dosing instructions for each medicine
Any supplements your pet takes
A cool pack or pouch if medicine needs it
items.note: Do not include human medicines unless your vet directs

items.text: Several days of food in a sealed container
Bottled water for each pet
Collapsible food and water bowls
A manual can opener if using canned food
Treats to reduce stress during an emergency
Copies of vaccination and medical records
Microchip number and registration details
A current photo of you with your pet
Vet and emergency hospital contact details
A list of medications and feeding instructions
A sturdy carrier or crate for transport
Spare leash, collar, and ID tags
Waste bags, litter, and a small litter tray
A blanket, towel, and a familiar toy
A flashlight and batteries for night use
Label the kit and store it where you can grab it
Check expiry dates a few times a year
Replace used or outdated supplies promptly
Update records, photos, and medications
Keep a copy of this list inside the kit
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; a kit supports but does not replace professional care, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: In any emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: What should be in a pet first aid kit?
faq.a: Common items include gauze, non-stick bandages, adhesive tape, blunt scissors, tweezers, a digital thermometer, gloves, saline, and a pet-safe wound cleaner. Add anything your vet recommends for your specific pet.

faq.q: How much food and water should a pet go-bag hold?
faq.a: Many guides suggest several days of food and water for each pet, stored in sealed containers. Adjust the amount to your pet's size and rotate it before it expires so supplies stay fresh.

faq.q: What records should I keep in the kit?
faq.a: Pack copies of vaccination and medical records, your pet's microchip number, a current photo, your vet's contact details, and medication instructions. These help with boarding, identification, and care if you are separated.

faq.q: How often should I check my pet emergency kit?
faq.a: Review it a few times a year. Replace expired food, water, and medicine, update records and photos, and confirm the bag still fits your pet's current needs and size.

faq.q: Is this pet emergency kit checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, check off each item as you pack, and tape a copy inside the kit so you can restock it easily.
